one_liner: Senior administrative and management services expert for ICE Homeland Security Investigations offices, running office operations, studying program changes, and advising managers.
fit_summary: The job is open to the public through Direct Hire. GS-13 requires a year of GS-12-level experience in all three areas: managing office administrative services, evaluating administrative programs for efficiency, and advising managers on complex issues. Daniel handled office manager duties at IEM (security, IT triage, travel support, help with onboarding and offboarding) and holds a Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt, but at a support level rather than GS-12 program management, so GS-13 is a reach.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and to federal transition (CTAP/ICTAP) candidates; no federal status is needed, and veterans' preference does not apply under Direct Hire.

You need at least one year of specialized experience at the GS-12 equivalent that includes all three listed areas: managing administrative and management services, evaluating administrative programs and systems, and giving authoritative advice to supervisors and managers.
You must meet all qualifications by the 11/03/2026 closing date, and your claims will be verified.
The security clearance is listed as 'Other'. Expect a DHS/ICE background investigation and suitability review.
No degree is required; this posting qualifies applicants on experience only.
keywords: essential to the operations of the office
evaluation of administrative programs, systems and methods
strategy: Before applying, preview the questionnaire at the posting's link and honestly rate yourself against each GS-12-level task. If you can't claim 'expert' on the three core areas, consider GS-11/12 Management and Program Analyst or Mission Support postings instead.

Frame your IEM work in your own words, without copying the posting. Show any office or project operations you managed, program or process evaluations you did for government clients, and advice you gave client managers on sensitive emergency-management issues.
Emphasize policy analysis: tie your knowledge of legislation and public policy to the 'conduct studies on new requirements in program operations, legislation, or agency regulations' duty.
Keep the resume to two pages. For each job, list exact start and end dates (month/year), hours per week, your title, and two to four specialized-experience bullets.
The window is only 10/30 to 11/03/2026. Have your resume, and transcripts if relevant, ready before the posting opens, and submit early.
Include relevant volunteer or civic work, such as campaign or community roles, since it counts and can strengthen your stakeholder and advising experience.
resume_bullets: Handled office manager duties at IEM (2019–2024): office security, first-line IT troubleshooting, deliveries and conference supplies, and help with onboarding and offboarding.
Answered employee travel-expense questions in Certify and booked flights for corporate-level staff.
Built Excel pivot-table reports on spending and order status for multi-state COVID-19 operations (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you evaluated an administrative process and improved its efficiency.
Describe a time you advised a senior manager on a sensitive issue they disagreed with you about.
How would you analyze a new regulation or legislative change and explain its impact on office operations?
Give an example of juggling competing priorities across multiple stakeholders.
watch_outs: The application window is only about five days.
The GS-13 specialized experience bar is high, and you must demonstrate all three elements or you will be rated ineligible. Overstating your experience can get you removed from consideration.
Expect a background investigation for ICE/HSI. 'Multiple locations' may include duty stations outside the National Capital Region, so check the location list carefully.
